title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Purpose
This playbook documents Redwood Inference’s standard hiring, onboarding, performance management, and manager responsibilities. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, and people-ops partners. Use this as the canonical process for role planning, candidate evaluation, offer workflows, new hire ramp, and performance cycles.

Quick links
- Hiring request form: /tools/hiring-requests
- Interview scorecard template: /templates/interview-scorecard
- New hire checklist (30/60/90): /templates/new-hire-checklist
- Performance review rubric: /templates/perf-review-rubric

1) Hiring: end-to-end process overview
Summary
- Goal: hire high-quality candidates with consistent candidate experience, predictable timelines, and equitable evaluation.
- Primary SLAs: time-to-fill target = 45 calendar days; time-to-offer target = 10 business days after final onsuite; interview feedback turnaround = 3 business days.

Steps (numbered)
1. Role approval and requisition
   - Hiring manager submits a hiring request with role justification, top responsibilities, target compensation band (PE/comp), org head approval. People-ops will create a requisition in the ATS within 2 business days.
2. Sourcing and screening
   - Recruiter builds a sourcing plan (internal referral, job boards, agency if needed).
   - Initial phone screen by recruiter: 30–45 minutes to assess role interest, compensation alignment, high-level skills, work authorization.
3. Interview loop design
   - Standard loop for IC roles: Recruiter screen -> Hiring manager technical screen -> 2 technical interviews (system design or take-home) -> bar raiser/peer interview -> hiring manager debrief.
   - Standard loop for manager roles: Recruiter screen -> Hiring manager screen -> leadership interview -> cross-functional partner interview -> case study or presentation -> debrief.
   - Interviewers must use the scorecard and capture evidence for each competency.
4. Offer and negotiation
   - Comp range confirmed with people-ops compensation partner. Typical turnaround: initial verbal offer within 48 business hours of decision; written offer packet in 3 business days.
   - Approval chain: Hiring manager -> Org Lead -> People Ops (comp) -> Finance (if > band) -> Legal (for senior IC/exec).
5. Background checks and reference checks
   - Completed after verbal acceptance. Use our approved vendor (vendor-check.example.com). Allow up to 7 business days.
6. Close and feedback
   - All candidates who interviewed must receive feedback within 5 business days of final decision. Collect interview loop notes for calibration records.

Interview scorecards and calibration
- Scorecards must map to 5 competencies: Role fit, Core skills, Problem solving, Collaboration & Communication, Impact & Ownership. Each competency uses a 1–5 scale with required narrative evidence for scores <=2 or >=4.
- Calibration sessions: Monthly for high-volume teams and quarterly for smaller teams. Calibration owners: hiring manager + people-ops partner.

2) Offer approvals and compensation guardrails
- Standard bands are published in the compensation matrix. People-ops must approve any offer above midpoint + 10%.
- Equity and signing bonuses require Director-level approval for IC roles and VP-level for manager roles.
- Approvals are recorded in ATS (requisition approval log).

3) New hire onboarding: 30/60/90 playbook
Intro
- Objective: get new hires productive and integrated while ensuring compliance and alignment to expectations. People-ops partners the hiring manager to deliver the experience.

Preboarding (before day 1)
- Tasks owner timeline:
  - IT: create laptop order and VPN credentials (complete 5 business days before start)
  - Security: schedule account provisioning & SSO (complete 3 business days before start)
  - Hiring manager: send welcome email with agenda and first-week goals (2 business days before start)
  - People-ops: send benefits enrollment packet and payroll forms (immediately after offer acceptance)

Day 1 checklist (sample)
- HR welcome + policies (1 hour): benefits overview, code of conduct, confidentiality, data handling basics.
- IT setup (2 hours): laptop build, SSO sign-in, email, Slack, calendar, developer VPN, repo access request.
- Team welcome & context (1 hour): intro meeting, product overview, key contacts.
- 30-minute manager 1:1 to align ramp plan.

First week (goals)
- Complete compliance trainings: security-awareness, data-privacy, acceptable-use (SLO: complete within 7 days).
- Access to dev environments and sandbox (SLO: within 14 days).
- Shadow calls and read core docs: runtime architecture, deployment playbook, onboarding knowledge base.

30/60/90 objectives (example)
- 30-day: complete onboarding checklist, merge first small PR, review relevant architecture docs, establish recurring 1:1 with manager.
- 60-day: own a small project, present a summary to peer team, complete role-specific trainings.
- 90-day: deliver a project milestone, demonstrate cross-team collaboration, agree on next growth goals and career plan.

Manager responsibilities during ramp
- Weekly 1:1s for first 90 days with explicit agenda and action items.
- Introductions to 8–12 critical partners.
- Clear success criteria and a 90-day written plan shared to the new hire.

Onboarding exceptions and escalation
- If laptop or access delays exceed 5 business days from start, escalate to IT manager and people-ops.
- If ramp milestones not met by 60 days, schedule a development check with people-ops partner.

4) Performance and feedback cycles
Cadence and cycle overview
- Annual cycle: goal-setting period (Jan 1–Jan 31), mid-year check-in (Jun 1–Jun 15), year-end review (Dec 1–Dec 20).
- Promotion and compensation review windows: mid-year (June) and year-end (Dec).
- Continuous feedback: expected behaviors include weekly manager feedback and quarterly peer feedback rounds.

Manager playbook for reviews
- Before the review window: calibrate with peer managers and people-ops to align ratings and remove bias. Use the calibration rubric.
- Writing reviews: provide specific examples tied to the rubric (impact, scope, leadership behaviors). Avoid vague language.
- Goal setting: each goal must be SMART and map to one of our company themes (reliability, performance, developer experience).

Performance rating scale and definitions
- Exceeds Expectations (5): Consistently delivers outsized impact; demonstrates leadership beyond role.
- Meets Expectations (3): Consistently meets goals and role expectations.
- Improvement Needed (2): Not meeting key expectations; requires targeted support.
- Unsatisfactory (1): Significantly below expectations; immediate remediation required.

Performance improvement plans (PIP)
- Use PIP when documented performance concerns persist after coaching (typical duration: 60–90 days).
- PIP owner: manager + people-ops. Outline specific measurable objectives, resources, expected outcomes, progress checkpoints (every 2 weeks), and final review date.
- Legal/HR escalation: people-ops alerts legal for senior-level PIPs or potential separations.

Calibration and fairness
- Use anonymized examples where feasible during calibration. Document justification for ratings and keep records for 3 years. People-ops audits random samples quarterly to check for rating drift and bias.

5) Feedback culture and best practices
- Feedback frequency: real-time praise/flag within 48 hours; structured feedback in weekly 1:1s and quarterly peer reviews.
- Feedforward model: focus on future actions and clear, actionable suggestions.
- Feedback checklist for managers: be specific, describe impact, offer concrete next steps, align on timeline.

6) Manager guide: hiring-to-ramp checklist
- Before hiring: define success metrics for role, top 3 outcomes in first 6 months, and interview rubric.
- During hiring: ensure interviewers have scorecards, calibrate after each loop, debrief within 48 business hours.
- Offer stage: confirm comp approvals and communicate growth path in the offer.
- Preboarding: prepare team agenda, assign onboarding buddy, create initial 30/60/90 plan.
- First 90 days: weekly 1:1s, document accomplishments, escalate blockers early.

7) Templates and examples (appendix)
- Sample interview scorecard (text):
  - Candidate: [name]
  - Role: [role]
  - Competencies: Role fit (1–5), Technical depth (1–5), Problem solving (1–5), Communication (1–5), Ownership (1–5)
  - Narrative evidence: [required for 1,2,4,5]
- Sample 30/60/90 email to new hire (text snippet):
  - Subject: Welcome to Redwood — Your 30/60/90 plan
  - Body: Hi [name], attached is your 30/60/90 plan. Expect weekly 1:1s with [manager], intro meetings with [X], and a first deliverable due at 30 days.

8) Metrics and reporting
- People-ops dashboard KPIs: time-to-fill, time-to-offer, acceptance rate, attrition (12-month), new-hire ramp (measured by % of hires hitting first milestone at 90 days), diversity of candidate funnel.
- Targets: acceptance rate >= 70%; new-hire ramp success (first milestone met) >= 85%; interview-to-offer ratio target <= 6.

9) Escalations and exceptions
- Hiring freeze: People ops will notify teams and place holds on active requisitions; approved exceptions require VP People sign-off.
- Failed background check: Follow the legal guidance; people-ops consults hiring manager and legal to determine next steps.

Ownership and governance
- Document owner: People Ops (Aisha Patel).
- Review cadence: annual review in Nov with updates applied by Dec 15.
- Audit: People-ops runs a semi-annual audit of hiring and review outcomes; findings are summarized to the exec team.
